items.question: Which goddesses are identified as great knowledges alongside Tārā?
premises: Tārā is named explicitly.

items.inference: Tārā and Tripurasundarī are both counted among the great knowledges.
items.plain_english: Tārā indeed is a great knowledge, and likewise Tripurasundarī.

items.question: Which additional goddesses are enumerated in address to the beloved?

items.plain_english: Tvaritā and Annapūrṇā, and likewise Vāgvādinī, O beloved.

items.plain_english: Dhūmāvatī and Bhairavī, and likewise Pratyaṅgirā and others.

Their recitation mantra is employed.

items.inference: Recitation of these goddesses' mantras causes the breaking of sleep.
items.plain_english: By reciting the mantras of these goddesses, sleep is broken.

rows.grounds: interrogative particle introducing a rhetorical question

items.question: Does continued recitation and worship of these goddesses cause any harm?
premises: The practice concerns recitation and worship of these goddesses.
The question asks about possible harm.

items.plain_english: What harm could there be in their recitation and worship? It becomes higher and higher.

rows.grounds: compound referring to Satya and subsequent ages
compound denoting the cycle of four ages

items.question: For whom and in which ages is Kālikā accessible as a deity?
premises: The context spans the four ages beginning with Satya.
The context includes all classes.

items.inference: Kālikā is accessible in all four ages and among all classes.
items.plain_english: In the four ages beginning with Satya, and among all classes, there is Kālikā.

items.question: What promise is made regarding the means to attain success with Kālikā?
premises: The speaker intends to tell the means.
The means pertain to that context.

items.plain_english: There I shall tell the means by which success arises.

items.question: How certain and timely is the attainment of success through these means?
premises: Success arises after a long time.
The arising of success is affirmed.

items.plain_english: Then success arises after a long time; there is no doubt about this.

items.plain_english: Recitation and worship of these goddesses is always commended, O one praised by heroes.

rows.grounds: compound denoting devotion to the guru

items.question: Under what condition does devotion to the guru arise in the practitioner?
premises: Devotion to the guru is the outcome in question.

items.plain_english: O fortunate one, O mother, devotion to the guru arises, if it may be.
